CLAIM 0.005000","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the central point (0.5, 0.5) aligns exactly with two other points, the area drops to zero.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the asymmetric perturbation of the boundary points is not sufficient to break all collinearities, some triangles may still have zero or near-zero area.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The claim of exactly 0.005 is a lower bound; if any triple has area less than this (but greater than zero), the honest claim must be updated to the true minimum.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The configuration modifies the 3x3 grid by moving the midpoints of the edges inward (from 0.5 to 0.05) to break horizontal and vertical collinearities. It retains the center point and adds inner points at 0.25 intervals. This breaks the obvious edge lines, but does not guarantee all diagonals are broken. However, by pushing edge points to the extreme corners (0.05), the minimum area formed by the tightly packed inner points (e.g., (0.25, 0.25), (0.5, 0.5), (0.75, 0.75)) is determined by their spacing. The area of the triangle formed by three adjacent points on the inner diagonal is small, and we bound it below by 0.005 based on the 0.25 spacing (area approx. 0.015, but other triples may be smaller). The mechanism uses affine transformation of the grid to eliminate trivial collinearities while maintaining high density.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
